{{Short description|Anglo-American mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''George Baron''' (died June 18, 1818) was a [[mathematician]] who emigrated from [[Northumberland]], [[England]] to [[Hallowell, Maine]] in the [[United States]], thereafter moving to [[New York (state)|New York]].  He was the first superintendent and mathematics professor at what would become the [[United States Military Academy]] in 1801<ref>{{cite book |last1=Park |first1=Roswell |title=A Sketch of the History and Topography of West Point and the U. S. Military Academy |url=https://archive.org/details/sketchofhistoryt00park |year=1840 |location=Philadelphia |page=[https://archive.org/details/sketchofhistoryt00park/page/138 138] }}</ref> and the founder and editor-in-chief of the ''[[Mathematical Correspondent]]'', which was the first American "specialized scientific journal"<ref>{{cite book |last1=Wagoner Jr. |first1=Jennings L. |last2=McDonald |first2=Christine Coalwell |editor1-first=Robert M.S. |editor1-last=McDonald |title=Thomas Jefferson's Military Academy: Founding West Point. |year=2004 |publisher=[[University of Virginia Press]] |isbn=0-8139-2298-4 |page=151 n. 45  |chapter=Mr. Jefferson's Academy: An Educational Interpretation. }}</ref> and the first American [[mathematics journal]], first published May 1, 1804.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cajori |first1=Florian|author-link1=Florian Cajori |title=The Teaching and History of Mathematics in the United States. |url=https://archive.org/details/teachingandhist03cajogoog |year=1890 |publisher=[[United States Government Printing Office|Government Printing Office]] |location=Washington|page=[https://archive.org/details/teachingandhist03cajogoog/page/n100 94]}}</ref>

Baron was first offered the position at the fledgling academy at [[West Point, New York]] by the newly elected [[United States President]] [[Thomas Jefferson]]'s [[United States Secretary of War|Secretary of War]] [[Henry Dearborn]], a friend of Baron's who had lived near him in Maine.  After agreeing upon salary and perks, instruction began on September 21, 1801 employing the use of [[Charles Hutton]]'s ''A Course in Mathematics'' and a [[blackboard]], the first recorded use of the latter in America.  In October, there was a disagreement between Baron and one of the cadets, [[Joseph Gardner Swift]]. Swift was called upon to apologize and was reprimanded for the language he employed against Baron, but went on to become the Military Academy's first graduate, and later a [[Brigadier General]].  For a variety of reasons, Baron was [[court-martialled]] in December, and [[Jonathan Williams (engineer)|Major Jonathan Williams]] became the supervisor and Captain William Amherst Barron became the instructor of mathematics.
<ref>{{cite journal |last=Rickey |first=V. Frederick |author2=Amy Shell-Gellasch |author2-link=Amy Shell-Gellasch|year=2008 |title=Mathematics Education at West Point: The First Hundred Years
 |journal=Loci |volume=1 |publisher=[[National Science Digital Library]] and [[Mathematical Association of America]]
 |editor1-first=Victor J. |editor1-last=Katz |editor1-link=Victor J. Katz |editor2-first=Frank J. |editor2-last=Swertz|issn=1941-9198 |access-date=14 Jan 2011 |url=http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/46/?pa=content&sa=viewDocument&nodeId=2590 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080803041608/http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/46/?pa=content&sa=viewDocument&nodeId=2590 |archive-date=3 August 2008 }}</ref>

Baron became a teacher of mathematics in [[New York City]], there joining the Deistical Society of New York,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Wood |first1=John |title=A Full Exposition of the Clintonian Faction |url=https://archive.org/details/fullexpositionof00wood|date= September 1802 |location=Newark |page=[https://archive.org/details/fullexpositionof00wood/page/31 31] }}</ref> a [[deist]] group led by [[Elihu Palmer]] that came to public attention in the course of a pamphlet war between supporters of [[United States Vice President]] [[Aaron Burr]] and supporters of then [[United States Senator]] from New York [[DeWitt Clinton]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Baker|first=Thomas N.|year=2008|title=Speculations on the Genealogy of Deism in New York, 1700–1850|journal=New York History|volume=89|issue=1|publisher=[[New York State Historical Association]]|issn=0146-437X|access-date=14 Jan 2011|url=http://www.historycooperative.org/journals/nyh/89.1/baker.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100328215103/http://www.historycooperative.org/journals/nyh/89.1/baker.html|archive-date=2010-03-28|url-status=dead}}</ref>
